tools.name: search_tutors
tools.description: Search iTutorOnline's verified tutor directory. Filter by subject/keyword, country, spoken language, max hourly price (EUR), and minimum rating. Returns ranked tutor cards with rates, ratings, and profile links.

tools.name: get_tutor
tools.description: Get the full public profile for one tutor: headline, description, subjects, academic levels, rate, rating, credentials, languages, and how to book. Identify the tutor by the id from a search_tutors result, or by the last part of their profile URL.

tools.name: get_tutor_reviews
tools.description: Get recent written reviews and the average score for a tutor.

tools.name: list_subjects
tools.description: List the subjects tutors teach, with the search terms and synonyms that match each. Use before search_tutors to pick a good subject term.

tools.name: get_platform_info
tools.description: Explain how iTutorOnline works: pricing, the free first 30 minutes, hour packages, languages of instruction, how booking works, and the live count of verified tutors.

tools.name: prepare_booking
tools.description: Assemble a real tutoring booking for a parent/student to finish in one tap. Give the tutor id, how long, who it is for, and optionally a preferred time. Returns a price estimate, a booking brief, and the link the human opens to confirm and pay. Creates nothing and charges nothing itself.

tools.name: request_human_tutor
tools.description: Hand a tutoring request to the iTutorOnline team so they can line up a human tutor. Requires the subject AND an email address the team can reply to — ask the student for one before calling this, because there is no other way to reach them afterwards. If they will not share an email, use search_tutor

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "get_tutor" references sensitive artifacts (credentials). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "request_human_tutor" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_tutor, get_tutor_reviews · Private data: get_tutor · Public sink: request_human_tutor.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_tutor, get_tutor_reviews · Private data: get_tutor · Public sink: request_human_tutor

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "get_tutor" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "Get the full public profile for one tutor by their user id (the id shown in search results or in a /tutor_profile/<id> URL): headline, description, subjects, academic levels, rate, rating, credentials, languages, and how to book." → after: "Get the full public profile for one tutor: headline, description, subjects, academic levels, rate, rating, credentials, languages, and how to book. Identify the tutor by the id from a search_tutors result, or by the last part of their profile URL."

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
